assistant.bannerText: Let a grow plan guide you through the stages — targets adjust automatically, and you confirm the big steps.

seedling.1: Keep the medium slightly moist, never soaking wet — seedlings drown faster than they dry out.
seedling.2: High humidity (65–75 %) helps young roots; a propagator dome works great in the first days.
seedling.3: Keep the light dimmed (around 40 %) and at a good distance — bleached or curled leaves mean it's too strong.
seedling.4: Don't feed yet: the seed carries nutrients for the first two weeks.

vegetative.1: Water when the top few centimeters of the medium feel dry — lifting the pot tells you more than a schedule.
vegetative.2: Now is training time: topping or bending (LST) creates an even canopy and more bud sites.
vegetative.3: Raise light intensity step by step towards 80–100 % as the plants toughen up.
vegetative.4: Watch the VPD chart: 0.8–1.1 kPa keeps transpiration and growth in balance.

flowering.1: Keep humidity at or below 50 % — dense buds plus high humidity is how mold starts.
flowering.2: Don't change the light schedule anymore; interruptions of the dark period stress photoperiod plants.
flowering.3: Feed bloom nutrients and watch leaf color — fading towards the end is normal.
flowering.4: Check the trichomes in the last weeks: cloudy with the first amber ones usually means harvest time.

drying.1: 16–20 °C and 55–60 % humidity, dark and with gentle air movement — slow drying preserves the terpenes.
drying.2: Plan for 10–14 days. If it's done after 5, it was too warm or too dry.
drying.3: The snap test: when small branches crack instead of bending, the buds are ready for curing jars.
drying.4: Open the jars daily in the first curing week ('burping') to let moisture escape.

control.noClimateNote: A plan step writes a climate — day and night targets, the CO₂ target, the light's limit — and this device states none of them. Its sockets and its output are on the Devices tab.
control.noClimateHasPlan: This device states no climate, so what these steps write lands in a document that has nowhere for it. A step whose settings are emptied sends nothing at all, and a stopped plan sends nothing until it is started again.
control.waitingHasPlan: This controller has not sent its settings yet, so these steps are held back rather than sent. What a step carries would not be added to the controller's own tuning but put in place of it: the work mode, the light schedule, the dehumidifier's timings and the dimming ramps would all be back at a factory value, and none of them has ever reached the cloud to be put back. A step whose settings are emptied sends nothing at all, and a stopped plan sends nothing until it is started again.

ask.extend: More time on the step the place is on. The step keeps the length it was written with and only its clock is put back, so a step that had already asked to be confirmed asks again when the longer time is up.
ask.skip: The plan moves on to step {{number}}, {{name}}, and starts its clock. What this step still had to run is not kept.
ask.skipPaused: The plan moves on to step {{number}}, {{name}}, and stays paused: that step's clock starts when the plan is resumed. What this step still had to run is not kept.
ask.skipEnds: This is the last step, so skipping it completes the plan. The controller keeps the settings this step gave it.
ask.stop: The plan keeps its steps and stands at the first one again, ready to be started. The controller keeps the settings the last step gave it: stopping says nothing about what the place should be doing instead.
ask.remove: The plan and its steps are taken off this controller. The controller keeps whatever it was last set to, and what the plan wrote stays in the diary. Keep it as a template first to start from it again.

step.name: Name
step.stageNote: The stage is what the step puts the grow standing here into, with the day counter and the diary line that go with it. A step with no stage leaves the phase where it is.
step.openEndedNote: A step of no length runs until somebody moves it on by hand.
step.writesNothing: This step writes nothing: the controller keeps whatever it was running when the step began.
step.writesSections: A step writes the figures it is given into the controller's settings: the day and night targets, the CO₂ target and the light's limit. A figure left empty stays what the controller has, and so does everything else in the controller's settings.
step.writesSectionsNoCo2: A step writes the figures it is given into the controller's settings: the day and night targets and the light's limit. This controller reports no CO₂ sensor, so no CO₂ target is written — its firmware holds one at zero whatever it is told. A figure left empty stays what the controller has, and so does everything else in the controller's settings.
step.writesNowhere: This controller has not sent its settings yet, so this step is not sent to it. What it carries would be put in place of the controller's own tuning rather than added to it, and every setting this step does not name would be back at a factory value. Clearing these figures is how the step is taken off.
step.alsoWrites: This step also carries settings this screen does not edit ({{sections}}); they are kept as they are.
step.takeFromController: Take what the controller holds now
step.waitsNote: When its time is up the plan stands still and asks, rather than moving on by itself.

effect.newPlan: This controller is being run by nothing, so the plan is saved at rest. Starting it is a separate tap.
effect.atRest: This plan is not running, so saving moves nothing: starting it begins at step 1.
effect.empties: A plan without steps has nothing to run, so it stops and the controller keeps what the last step gave it.
effect.stays: The place goes on running {{name}} as step {{number}}, with the time it has already served.
effect.moves: {{name}} is the step the place is on: it moves from {{from}} to {{to}} and keeps the time it has already served.

leave.bodyKeepsRoom: You keep this place through {{room}} and give up only the role you held here. What you wrote here stays here and goes on carrying your name.

stream.tunnelOff: The cloud opens the stream itself, which only works for a camera reachable from the internet.

maintenance.pausesEach_other: For {{minutes}} minutes this pauses all {{count}} devices here:

sheet.fractionNote: As a fraction of the time it runs: 0.5 is half the time.
sheet.switchNote: Off or on, and nothing in between: 0 or 1.
sheet.ticksNote: How often the valve opened since the last reading, counted rather than measured — not a level.

sheet.forNote: How long the reading has to stay past the line before the alarm is raised. 0 raises it at once.

sheet.infoNote: An info alarm is written to the diary and never announced.

sheet.repeatNote: While it lasts, every so many minutes; 0 says it once.

sheet.deleteAsk: The rule is gone for good. An alert it has already raised stays in the inbox.
sheet.offlineWatch: This one watches whether the device reports at all, which is not something that can be pointed elsewhere.

health.notAnswered: Not here because this install answers no figure for them yet: MQTT connections as the broker counts them - online above is what has been heard from, not what is connected -, the size of the time-series database, the server's own log, and the alarms of the last seven days per device.
health.unclassified: {{devices}} in no class, which no rollout reaches
health.noDemo: No device is marked as a demo one

firmware.title: Firmware
firmware.classesHow: A channel points at a build, and every device of the class that follows that channel is told to install it. Nothing here is written until Apply, and what the change would reach stands under the controls.
firmware.willPoint: {{channel}} will point at {{build}}. That reaches {{devices}} on the channel, about {{reach}} in this stage, up to {{concurrent}} installing at a time.
firmware.willUnpoint: {{channel}} will point at no build. Nothing further is told to the {{devices}} on it.
firmware.willStage: The stage goes from {{from}} % to {{to}} %, which is about {{after}} rather than {{before}} {{ofDevices}}.
firmware.willPace: At most {{devices}} installing at once, and the rollout stops by itself after {{failures}}.
firmware.confirmBody: This reaches hardware standing in somebody's place, within minutes:
firmware.registerHow: A build is registered before it has any bytes; its files are uploaded against it afterwards. The version is the uuid the build container stamped it with, and is never compared with another.
firmware.inUse: A channel still points at this build. Point it elsewhere first.
firmware.uploadBody: A device asks for a file by the name it was built to ask for, so the name is part of the address. Uploading the same name again replaces what is there.
firmware.fileName: The name the device asks for
firmware.deleteBody: {{build}} and every file of it go. A device part way through installing it finds nothing left to fetch.
firmware.noBuilds: No build is registered on this install yet.

users.title: Users
users.noMatch: No account matches "{{search}}". The search reads handles and addresses.
users.privacy: An address is on this screen and on no other in the app. The search reads only what is already loaded, so nothing typed here is sent anywhere.
users.createBody: It is active at once and gets no activation code, so whoever makes it hands the password over.
users.changeSomebody: This is somebody else's account: @{{handle}}. What is changed here is changed for them, and they are told by nothing.
users.demoteMine: Without "May run this install" the Admin section is gone for you the moment this is saved, and you cannot give it back to yourself.
users.deactivateMine: Without "Active" this account cannot sign in at all, and it is the account you are signed in with.
users.lastAdmin: This is the only administrator this install has. Make somebody else one before taking it away here.
users.deleteBody: Everything @{{handle}} owns goes with the account: their places, grows, entries, pictures and films. What they wrote in other people's places stays there and loses their name. It cannot be taken back.
users.deleteAdmin: If this is the account the install is configured with, the server keeps it: that account is looked up by its address on every start and is not deleted from here.
users.deleteDevices: The devices they had claimed become claimable again by whoever is holding them.
users.deleteMine: This is your own account. Deleting it signs you out and leaves this install without you.

demo.title: Demo device
demo.what: What a demo visitor sees: every place, device, camera and grow marked as a demo object. Nothing on this screen writes - the mark is a property of the database with no route behind it, and is set where the demo is seeded.
demo.empty: Nothing on this install is marked as a demo object, so the demo tour has nothing to show.
demo.noDevice: No device is in the demo.
demo.noPlace: No place is in the demo.
demo.noGrow: No grow is in the demo.
demo.noCamera: No camera is in the demo.

diagnosis.title: Support view
diagnosis.settings: Settings, as sent to the device
diagnosis.noSettings: The device has no settings document yet.
diagnosis.noLines: The device has reported nothing yet.

status.invalid: The server did not accept that. Check what was entered and try again.
status.forbidden: You may not do that here.
status.missing: That is no longer there. Reload the page to see what is.
status.conflict: That cannot be done right now, because something changed in the meantime. Reload the page and try again.
status.tooMany: Too many attempts in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.
status.fault: The server ran into a fault. Please try again.

code.space_not_found: That place is not there any more, or you may not see it.
code.device_not_found: That device is not there any more, or you may not see it.
code.grow_not_found: That grow is not there any more, or you may not see it.
code.camera_not_found: That camera is not there any more, or you may not see it.
code.plant_not_found: That plant is not there any more.
code.entry_not_found: That line is not there any more.
code.task_not_found: That task is not there any more.
code.insufficient_access: You may read this but not change it.
code.space_archived: That place has ended. Bring it back before putting anything in it.
code.capability_not_announced: This device has not said it understands that. It needs newer firmware.
code.device_sent_no_settings: This device has not sent its settings yet, so there is nothing to write into.
code.device_states_no_climate: This device states no climate, so there is nowhere to write one.
code.task_done_already: That task has been ticked off already.
code.occurred_in_the_future: A line records something that has happened. It can be dated back but not forward.
code.too_many_requests: Too many attempts in a short time. Wait a minute and try again.

offline.power: Power: is the adapter plugged in, is the socket live?
offline.wifi: Wi-Fi and router: is the router on, does the signal reach the device?
offline.replug: Unplug the device, wait 10 seconds, plug it back in.
offline.keeps: The last readings stay until something arrives again.

vpd.title: VPD – vapour pressure deficit
vpd.text: How strongly the air draws water from the leaves, in kPa, worked out from humidity and leaf temperature (by default 2 °C below the air by day). It has no target of its own: it follows from the temperature and humidity targets.

liveness.title: Live and stale
liveness.text: Live: the newest reading is less than 2 minutes old. Stale: less than 10. After that the device counts as offline, and its figures are dimmed rather than hidden – they are the last thing it measured.

band.title: In band
band.text: Close enough to the target to count as on it: within ±1 °C, ±5 % humidity or ±200 ppm CO₂. At night CO₂ has no band, because the controller only adds CO₂ while the light is on.

verdict.title: In band over 24 hours
verdict.text: The share of the last 24 hours in which temperature, humidity and, by day, CO₂ were all in their band – judged against the targets as they are now. Dips shorter than 10 minutes count, but are not named.

climatePreset.title: Climate preset
climatePreset.text: A ready climate for a stage: day and night temperature and humidity, the light hours, the light limit and CO₂. Auto is for autoflowers, which keep 18–20 hours of light instead of going to 12/12.

stage.title: Stage and phase
stage.text: The stage is where the plants are, from germination to curing. Entering one writes a phase on the grow: the date it began, a diary line, and the stage's alarm rules on the devices where the plants stand (curing has none).

stepPreset.title: A preset in a step
stepPreset.text: Here a preset only names the phase more closely – Auto for an autoflower, Late flower for the last weeks. It sends no targets: the step writes the figures below and nothing else.

plan.title: Grow plan
plan.text: A list of steps, each a stage, a length and the targets the controller should hold. While it runs, the cloud moves on when a step's time is up and sends the current step's targets again every hour the controller is online.

planMoves.title: Start and pause
planMoves.text: Start sends step 1's targets to the controller within half a minute, if it is online, and puts the grow here into the step's stage if it names one. Pause stops the step's clock and sends nothing; the controller keeps the targets it has until the plan runs again.

dayNight.title: Day and night
dayNight.text: Day is while the light is on, not a time of day: the controller switches the lamp and the day and night targets together, and adds CO₂ only by day. Light on at sets when the day begins, Light on for how long it lasts.

lightLimit.title: Light limit
lightLimit.text: The most the lamp may give, as a share of its full output: it ramps up to it at sunrise and down again at sunset. 0 % keeps the lamp dark, as the drying preset does.

lightsOn.title: Light on at
lightsOn.text: When the light comes on and the day begins, on your account's clock (Me › Appearance). When the clocks change for summer or winter time it stays at this time - the cloud resets the device itself on the night of the change. For cheaper night power or a cooler summer tent, move the day into the night, from 22:00 for example.

resumePlan.title: Resume the plan
resumePlan.text: The plan's clock runs on from where it stopped, and within the hour the step's own figures are sent again, replacing those set here.

growDay.title: Grow day
growDay.text: Day 1 is the day the grow began, and each further day is another 24 hours from that moment. The counter starts with the first phase and stops when the grow ends.

growWeek.title: Week of the stage
growWeek.text: “Veg week 2” is the second week the grow has stood in veg. How far the grow is overall is said by the day: day 1 is the day it began. The week cards are named by their days and carry the week of the stage most of that week lay in.

autoTag.title: auto
autoTag.text: This phase was set by a grow plan or a climate preset, which wrote the targets here along with it – it was not recorded as a stage alone. It has nothing to do with autoflowers.

phasePreset.title: Targets with the phase
phasePreset.text: Leave as they are records only the phase: light, temperature and humidity stay as they are under Control. Choosing a climate switches the targets of the devices there right away – for Flower, for instance, the light goes to 12 hours. Auto is for autoflowers, which keep long days.

phaseCorrection.title: Correct or withdraw
phaseCorrection.text: Both change the record only: the phase's date, the day count it starts and its diary line. Neither puts back the targets or the light the controllers were given at the time.

autoflower.title: Photoperiod or autoflower
autoflower.text: A photoperiod plant flowers once the light goes to 12/12; an autoflower flowers by age and keeps long days. It is chosen here once: a grow started in Veg or Flower gets the Auto climate, and a feeding scheme runs at half strength with no flip week.

growEnds.title: Ending the grow
growEnds.text: Once the last plants are harvested the grow ends on this day: nothing can be dated after it, and it cannot be reopened in the app. Enter drying and curing first if they belong in the diary.

dayNightAverages.title: Day / night
dayNightAverages.text: Averages over the hours the light was on and the hours it was off, as the controller switched it – not by the clock. Where no light was recorded, one average is shown instead.

feedStrength.title: Strength
feedStrength.text: Scales every dose in the scheme – half strength halves them. The EC targets stay as the scheme gives them.

waterEc.title: Water
waterEc.text: The EC of your water before anything is added. It is added to the scheme's EC targets, so a target is what your meter should read; 0 means reverse osmosis water.

feedFlip.title: Flip week
feedFlip.text: The scheme is read by the grow's own week, counted from day 1. The flip week says when the grow went to 12/12 and marks the scheme's weeks from then on as flowering; it does not switch the light or enter a phase.

chartLayout.title: Layout
chartLayout.text: Stacked gives each measure a chart of its own; Overlay lays them on one chart and names any whose scale does not fit. Day-of-grow counts the axis in grow days instead of dates – with the Phase or Grow range – so an earlier grow of the same place can be laid over it.

muteAll.title: Mute all
muteAll.text: For an hour nothing is sent to you, critical alarms included, and alarm messages from that hour are not sent later. Only you are muted: the others you share your places with are still told, and a rule with its own e-mail or webhook still sends.

silence.title: Silence 1 h
silence.text: Stops this one rule telling anybody for an hour – every member, every channel, its own e-mail or webhook too. The rule keeps watching: the alert still shows under Alerts.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.text: For working in the tent or cabinet: for 15, 30 or 60 minutes the device stops the heater, the dehumidifier or compressor and the CO₂ valve, and dims the light. Alarms stay off 10 minutes longer, until the climate is back. Then everything carries on by itself; you can also end maintenance sooner.

reboot.title: Restart
reboot.text: Restarts the device – useful when it hangs or behaves oddly. It is usually offline for less than a minute and regulates nothing meanwhile. Targets and settings are kept; anything switched by hand ends.

endMaintenance.title: End now
endMaintenance.text: The device takes up its work again at once. Its alarms stay held for another 10 minutes while the climate comes back.

presetRules.title: Rules from the stage
presetRules.text: Each stage brings four rules – too hot, too humid, too cold at night and too much CO₂ – with lines worked out from the targets. The next stage moves their lines and waits; what you switched off, regraded or silenced stays, and curing removes them.

offlineRule.title: The offline rule
offlineRule.text: Every device has one rule that raises a critical alarm once nothing has been heard from it for ten minutes, plus the rule's own wait. It cannot be deleted – only switched off, silenced or sent elsewhere.

alarmTemplates.title: Set up in one tap
alarmTemplates.text: One tap writes an ordinary alarm rule. For temperature and humidity its line comes from your targets: 5 °C over the warmer one, 4 °C under the cooler one, 10 points of humidity over the higher one and 20 under the lower one. “CO₂ cylinder empty” speaks up under 350 ppm, less than outdoor air: with a cylinder on the valve, it has run empty. “Fridge runs without a break” speaks up when the compressor runs 30 minutes without a pause – usually a door left open, a broken seal or too much heat from the lamp. Every one is critical, so it goes out by your notification settings, quiet hours included. Tap the rule to change its line, how long it waits or anything else.

alarmQuiet.title: Muting and maintenance
alarmQuiet.text: A muted rule keeps watching: the alert still shows under Alerts and marks the place on Home – it only tells nobody. Maintenance mode holds the alarms themselves back: for its 15 minutes and 10 more, while the climate comes back.

severity.title: Severity
severity.text: Critical and warning go out on the matching rows of each person's notification settings, and only critical comes through quiet hours. Info is not announced there: it only shows under Alerts.

tellBy.title: Tell me by
tellBy.text: My notification settings reaches everyone who keeps this place, each by their own settings, mute and quiet hours. An e-mail address or a webhook reaches only that address, whatever anybody's mute or quiet hours.

routingGrid.title: What goes where
routingGrid.text: Each row is a kind of message, each column a way to reach you; nothing is sent until you switch a cell on. The grid is yours alone – everyone you share places with sets their own – and an alarm rule with its own e-mail or webhook does not go through it.

emailAlarms.title: Alarms by e-mail
emailAlarms.text: Until a way is set up, nothing reaches you: no alarm, not even “device offline”, no task that is due and no camera that stopped delivering. One tap sends what can call on you by e-mail to the address you sign in with: a device's critical alarms, a camera's warning and the reminders of your tasks. Everything else stays as it is. Change or switch it off under Me › Notifications. “Later” hides this notice for a week.

quietHours.title: Quiet hours
quietHours.text: Between these times only critical alarms reach you. Warnings and the news that an alarm is over are not sent later; tasks and plan questions arrive once the quiet hours end.

rhythms.title: Rhythms
rhythms.text: A reminder is the rule: each time it falls due it shows above as a task, and ticking the task off moves the reminder on to its next turn. The list above looks a week ahead.

rhythmEvery.title: Rhythm
rhythmEvery.text: Every N days counts from the last time it was ticked off, or from when it was set up – not from a calendar: ticking it early brings the next turn forward, and missed turns do not pile up. Once falls due at the start of that day.

taskFor.title: For
taskFor.text: For everyone: everybody who keeps the place is told when it falls due. For me: only you are.

socketRoles.title: Socket roles
socketRoles.text: Every smart socket is given a role at the device and switches with it: a heater socket with the heater, a light socket with the lamp, pump or timer by a cycle of its own, and a manual one only while you hold it. An exhaust runs from 0.8 °C over the target and stops just above it, a humidifier from 5 points of humidity under the target and stops at the target. The role is set when the socket is paired; it can be changed under Advanced in the socket.

socketHold.title: Hold
socketHold.text: A tap on the switch holds the socket in the other state for an hour; here you can hold it for longer, up to 24 hours. The hold lives in the device's memory: a restart ends it, and Back to auto ends it early.

findSocket.title: Find it
findSocket.text: Switches this socket on for two seconds and off again, so you can see which one it is. The controller puts it back as it should be within a minute – a lamp or a heater that was on may stay off until then.

lightHold.title: Auto, on, off
lightHold.text: On keeps the lamp lit at its light limit, at night too; Off keeps it dark – for the time shown or until the device restarts. The device does not report a hold back: what was last sent from here is marked until its time is up. Auto ends it.

firmwareChannel.title: Updates
firmwareChannel.text: Whether the device installs new firmware by itself. On: new stable versions arrive by themselves, with their fixes; under Advanced test versions (beta, alpha) can be chosen too. Off: it stays on the version it has. While an update installs, a controller or fridge module switches every output and socket off for a moment, then restarts.

stillCadence.title: Still every
stillCadence.text: How often the cloud asks this camera for a picture, 30 seconds at the least; after a failed try it waits twice as long each time, up to two hours. Older pictures are thinned: after a day one a minute is kept, after a week one every 5, after a month one every 15, after three months one an hour.

cameraPauses.title: Night off, off during maintenance
cameraPauses.text: Night off skips pictures while the device's light is off; off during maintenance skips them while the device is in maintenance or switched off. Both only work for a camera that belongs to a device, and with night off no warning is raised when this camera stops delivering.

staleWarning.title: Tells you
staleWarning.text: The warning comes once no picture has arrived for ten intervals, and ten minutes at the least – but not while its device is offline, which has an alert of its own. Logging failed captures writes a diary warning for every try that fails.

premiumCamera.title: Premium
premiumCamera.text: Premium belongs to one camera, not to the account, and never renews by itself; a Terp Cam comes with 12 months when it is first paired. Without it, films are SD with a watermark, and HD and whole-grow films are not made.

timelapses.title: Timelapses
timelapses.text: Films made from this camera's stored pictures, 25 to the second. The day, week and month films rebuild themselves; the chips film today, the last complete week, the current phase or the whole grow.

overlays.title: Overlays
overlays.text: What is drawn on the film: the grow's day, a temperature and humidity curve with the moment marked, and diary entries as captions. Each needs something to draw from – a grow, a device, entries – and is left out where there is none.

lightsOffFrames.title: Lights-off frames
lightsOffFrames.text: Left off, pictures taken while the device's light was off are dropped, so the film does not flash dark every night. A picture with no light reading counts as lit.

render.title: Render
render.text: HD is 1920 pixels on the long side and needs Premium; SD is 1280, with a watermark unless the camera has Premium. Rendering the same days again with other settings replaces the film made before.

unpair.title: Unpair
unpair.text: The cloud stops reading this camera; its pictures and films stay. A Terp Cam stays paired to its device, though, and comes back here the next time the device reports it, for example after a restart.

rtsp.title: RTSP
rtsp.text: The live video stream most network cameras offer, at an address that starts with rtsp://. The cloud takes a still from it at the camera's interval, as it does from a Terp Cam.

rolloutFailures.title: Failures that stop it
rolloutFailures.text: A device counts as failed once it was told to update and is not running the new build ten minutes later – offline devices included. At this many on a channel no further devices are told; the rollout carries on by itself once they report the build.

publicPage.title: Public page
publicPage.text: Anybody can read the diary at this address without an account – the phases, the week cards with their photos and the camera's pictures. The address is made from the grow's name, so it is not a secret; switching the page off takes it down at once.

linkActions.title: Change, revoke, forget
linkActions.text: Change sets a link's days, pictures and expiry anew – wider as well as narrower – and keeps its address. Revoke stops the address working at once and keeps it in this list with the day it stopped. Forget appears once a link has stopped, revoked or run out, and takes it off the list. Neither can be undone.

shareWindow.title: From, to, expires
shareWindow.text: From and To decide which days of the diary the reader sees; left empty, they start at the beginning and keep up with the diary. Expires is the day the address itself stops working, at the end of that day in your time zone.

spaceLink.title: Grow or place
spaceLink.text: A link to a place shows its live climate against the targets – once its To date has passed, the climate of its last day instead – the grows standing there – private ones too – and its latest diary lines; a link to a grow shows that grow's diary. Neither shows tasks or alerts.

privacyRedaction.title: Shared views
privacyRedaction.text: These hide figures from everyone who reads through a link, your public page or a follow. People you let into a place are not strangers: they still see weights and counts.

publicProfile.title: Public profile
publicProfile.text: Your profile page lists your public grows with your bio and picture. Switched off, the page is gone, but your username still shows on each public grow.

deleteAccount.title: Deleting the account
deleteAccount.text: Everyone you let into your places loses access, and followers lose your grows. Lines you wrote in other people's places stay, without your name, and the climate readings stay with the devices, which can then be claimed again.

passwordChange.title: Changing the password
passwordChange.text: Every other browser and app signed in as you is signed out; this one stays signed in.

memberRole.title: Roles
memberRole.text: Can log may write entries, add photos and tick off tasks. Can manage may also change targets, plans, alarm rules, sockets and camera settings, and correct other people's entries; inviting, removing people and share links stay with you as the owner.

invite.title: Inviting
invite.text: Anybody who has an invite link can join with it, as often as it is used, until it expires or you revoke it – revoking stops new joins, and whoever is in stays. A username you already share a place with is added at once as can log, without being asked.

diaryLayer.title: Grow diary
diaryLayer.text: The diary is where you keep what you do to your plants – watering, feeding, photos, notes – and run grows with days and phases. While you do not use it, the app shows the climate and the device alone. It switches itself on once you start a grow or log something, and puts “Log” in the middle of the bar; under Me › Appearance you can also switch it on or off by hand.

follow.title: Follow
follow.text: Puts this grow on your home for as long as it is public. The grower is not told who follows, and nothing is sent to you when it changes.

compressor.title: Compressor
compressor.text: In the fridge module one compressor both cools and dries: while it runs, temperature and humidity fall together. That is why it is listed under both readings – it is one machine, not two.

dayCurve.title: The last 24 hours
dayCurve.text: The small curve shows how the reading went over the last 24 hours. The grey stretch is the night, the green band the target range – at night the night target applies, which is why the band steps with the light. Tapping the tile opens the Timeline.

ppfd.title: PPFD
ppfd.text: How much light the plant can use arrives at leaf level, in µmol per square metre and second. It is estimated from the sensor's lux reading with the factor set for your device.

leafTemperature.title: Leaf temperature
leafTemperature.text: How warm the leaves themselves are, measured by the leaf sensor. Under the light they usually sit a little below the air, because they evaporate water – that is what the VPD is worked out from. There is no target of its own: the leaves follow the air and the light.

lux.title: Light intensity
lux.text: How bright it is at the light sensor, in lux. The curve shows when and how strongly the lamp shines. How much of it the plant can use is the PPFD, which is estimated from the lux.

deviceOffer.title: Device or camera
deviceOffer.text: A controller or a fridge module measures temperature and humidity by itself, steers heating, light and fans, and tells you when something is wrong. A camera takes pictures for the diary and for timelapses. You add either through this line or under Me › Add a device or a camera. “No thanks” hides this line on all your devices.

schemeWeek.title: Scheme week
schemeWeek.text: A feeding scheme counts weeks from the grow's first day, not from the start of a stage: scheme week 3 is days 15–21. That is why it can differ from “veg week 2”. The doses on the Feed tile and on the week card are that week's.

climateControl.title: Control
climateControl.text: Switches the device's whole climate control off and on again: heater, cooling or dehumidifying, light, CO₂ and fans. While it is off the device keeps measuring and reporting. Meant for an empty cabinet, for cleaning or for the time between two grows. Saving targets, applying a preset or the next plan step switches control back on.

energySaving.title: Energy saving
energySaving.text: With large plants and a lot of plant mass it can save energy not to run the back-wall fan all the time: it then rests while the compressor is off. Try it out. If the fridge then runs too long at a stretch, or the lamp dims because it gets too warm, switch the mode off again. As a rule of thumb, switch it on once the heater has to run constantly during the day.

operatingMode.title: Operating mode
operatingMode.text: What the fridge does as a whole while control is on. Standard holds temperature, humidity, light and CO₂. Greenhouse holds the temperature only: light and CO₂ keep running, the compressor only cools and does not dehumidify on purpose. Germination keeps it dark and heats and cools to the night temperature. Energy saving applies to standard only. A drying phase takes precedence and returns to the operating mode afterwards.

chartStep.title: Interval
chartStep.text: Each point of a curve is the mean over this interval. Automatic fits it to the window. Shorter intervals show more detail, longer ones smooth. An interval too short for the window is drawn at the shortest that fits - at most 5000 points a curve.

chartVpdHalf.title: VPD by day or night
chartVpdHalf.text: Day and night are steered to different VPD values, so one line across both looks like a saw. Here you draw only the day or only the night values. What counts as day is what the light says, as for the shading of the curves.

chartLive.title: Update automatically
chartLive.text: The charts reload every 30 seconds and move on with the time - handy with the page open beside the device. A window stepped back, zoomed or picked by hand stands still.

cameraTunnel.title: Pull through the device
cameraTunnel.text: On, the cloud pulls the stream from your home network over the connection of the device in this place, so the camera needs no port forwarding and no dynamic DNS. Turn it off only for a camera reachable from the internet: the cloud then opens the stream itself, and the device's connection is left alone.

cameraTransport.title: Transport
cameraTransport.text: How the stream is read. TCP is right for almost every camera. HTTP or HTTPS only where the camera offers RTSP tunnelled through HTTP alone. UDP only for a camera the cloud reaches directly; it does not pass through the device. Where no picture comes, try another setting and then “Take a picture now”.

release.title: Give the device up
release.text: Takes the device out of your account so someone else can add it – after a sale, a move to another account or a swap. Its grow plan, its alarms and the camera connected through it go with it. The place and the diary stay, and nothing changes on the device itself.

updateChannel.title: Update channel
updateChannel.text: Which channel the device installs new firmware from by itself. Stable gets released versions only. Beta gets test versions before everyone else, alpha earlier ones still. Test versions can have faults a stable one does not.

firmwarePin.title: Firmware version
firmwarePin.text: Puts one device on a particular build, for example to roll back after a faulty release or to give one customer a test build. The device stays on it until somebody switches automatic updates back on.

pairSocket.title: Pair a socket by IP
pairSocket.text: Pairs a Tasmota socket with this device by its address on the local network. The role says what it switches with: the heater, the dehumidifier, the CO₂, the light – or by a cycle of its own as a pump or an own timer. A Terp Control socket is paired on the device itself.

editSocket.title: Change a socket
editSocket.text: Rarely needed: the device finds its sockets again by their hardware id, even when the router gives them new addresses. Address, role and credentials can be changed; empty credentials keep what the socket has.

removeSocket.title: Remove a socket
removeSocket.text: The device forgets the socket and resets it. It then no longer switches along and leaves the list. Only works while the device is connected.

co2Dosing.title: CO₂ dosing
co2Dosing.text: Throughout opens the valve whenever the reading drops below the switch-on point. In intervals, the socket doses only in one window of every interval – for example 10 minutes every hour – so a fan can be slowed during that time.

co2Fan.title: Slow an AIR fan
co2Fan.text: While the socket doses in intervals, an AIR fan runs at the set speed at most, so the CO₂ is not blown out again right away. The fan knows the socket's dosing windows for it; when its interval changes, the fan is told.

plugProtections.title: Protections
plugProtections.text: Switch the socket off whatever it is regulating: above a temperature, below a temperature, and they keep least times on and off so an appliance does not switch every few seconds. It comes back on only once the reading is back by the set gap.

lightRamp.title: Sunrise and sunset
lightRamp.text: How many minutes the light takes to come up in the morning and go down in the evening, 0 to 60. Fifteen minutes suits almost every lamp. 0 switches it hard – for drivers that flicker at low dimming levels.

maintenanceLight.title: Light on during maintenance
maintenanceLight.text: By day maintenance dims the light to 15 % anyway. Switched on, it also runs at 15 % during the dark period, so you can see what you are doing at night. In flower, light in the dark period disturbs the plants – leave it off then.

fans.title: Fans
fans.text: The clip fan moves the leaves: seedlings do not like it at full strength, and at night the noise counts. 0 % stops it. The inner fans move the air around the cabinet; the figure is the least they run at, and they speed up when they need to. They do not go below 10 %.

compressorRest.title: Compressor rest
compressorRest.text: How long the compressor stays off at least before it may start again, which protects it from short-cycling. It cannot be less than 240 seconds; more makes the control slower, because cooling and dehumidifying have to wait longer.

leafOffset.title: Leaf against air
leafOffset.text: How much warmer or cooler than the air the leaf is taken to be wherever no leaf sensor measures it. That is what VPD is worked out with on Start, in History and on the targets. Under light a leaf evaporates water and is cooler: the default is −2 °C by day and 0 °C at night. Nothing is regulated by it.

ppfdFactor.title: Lux to PPFD factor
ppfdFactor.text: Turns the light sensor's lux into PPFD. The right factor depends on the lamp's spectrum: white full-spectrum LED about 0.015, high-pressure sodium (HPS) about 0.0122. With the wrong one the PPFD shown is up to 20 % off.

continuePlan.title: Continue the plan at a step
continuePlan.text: Puts the plan on a step of your choice: back to a step that ended too soon, or into the middle of a grow, straight into flower for instance. The step starts from the beginning, its values reach the device within a minute, and a grow in this place moves into its phase. A paused or stopped plan runs again afterwards.

co2Report.title: CO₂ cylinder
co2Report.text: When a cylinder goes in, note what it holds and – if you weighed it – what was left in the old one. From the valve openings the device counts, the card works out how many openings a gram of CO₂ is. From the first empty cylinder on it estimates what is left in the one in use and how long it will last.

lightOverheat.title: Overheat protection
lightOverheat.text: Above this temperature at the light module the lamp dims itself down until it is cooler again. That protects the lamp and the plants right under it.

installApp.title: App on the home screen
installApp.text: Terp Control needs no app store: the browser puts the page on the home screen as an app with its own icon. It then opens full-screen without an address bar, and you stay signed in. On an iPhone it is also the only way to push notifications, because Safari delivers them only to apps on the home screen.

alarmRepeat.title: Repeat
alarmRepeat.text: While the alarm lasts, it is said again every so many minutes - for a warning or a notice just as for a critical alarm. That helps above all a webhook that switches something at home: if one call is lost, the next one comes. 0 says it once.

webhookTemplate.title: Webhook template
webhookTemplate.text: For Home Assistant, Discord, Telegram and ntfy the template fills in the URL, method and messages from the few answers the service needs. What is saved is an ordinary webhook, which you can still change by hand. A Home Assistant address on the local network is called through the device's tunnel automatically.

chartZoom.title: Zoom
chartZoom.text: “Zoom in” shows a third of the window around the cursor, at finer points. On a computer you can also mark a stretch across the curves with the mouse button held down. “Reset zoom” shows the whole window again.

chartMessages.title: Messages
chartMessages.text: What was written over the window: the devices' messages, alarms, the grow plan and the diary. Each column stands for a stretch of the window and is as tall as the messages in it - yellow with a warning, red with something critical. Tap a column to read its messages alone; the cursor moves there too.

streamAddress.title: Stream address
streamAddress.text:
Where the camera offers its video stream, with its IP on your network (shown in your router or in the camera's app). Common addresses:
Tapo: rtsp://IP:554/stream1
Reolink: rtsp://IP:554/h264Preview_01_main
Hikvision: rtsp://IP:554/Streaming/Channels/101
User and password go into the fields below. For Tapo that is the camera account from the Tapo app (Camera Settings › Advanced Settings › Camera Account), not your TP-Link account. A Reolink camera needs RTSP switched on in its network settings.

stepLightHours.title: Light on for (in a step)
stepLightHours.text: How many hours a day the light is on while this step runs. It comes on at the usual time (“Light on at” under Targets) and goes off that many hours later. Twelve hours is what makes photoperiod plants flower. Left empty, the light keeps the hours it has.

readyPlans.title: Ready-made plans
readyPlans.text: Two whole grows for the fridge: photoperiod (about 16 weeks, flower starts with the switch to 12 hours of light) and autoflower (about 11 weeks, the light stays at 18 hours). Every step brings its phase's targets; before flower, before harvest and at the end of drying the plan waits for you. Choosing one opens the plan to look through; nothing is written until “Save plan”.

drying.title: Drying
drying.text: While drying the device knows no day and no night: the light stays off, no CO₂ is dosed, it only dehumidifies and heats to the drying targets. Drying starts with the “Drying” preset under Control, with the drying phase in the grow or with a drying plan step. It ends with “End drying”, another preset or another phase; the device then goes back to its operating mode, energy saving included.

socketTimer.title: Timer
socketTimer.text: A socket with the role Pump or Own timer switches by its own cycle, not by the climate: for example on for 2 minutes, every 6 hours. Without a timer it stays off. The cycle keeps running on the device even when the connection to the cloud is gone.

plugMode.title: Switches by
plugMode.text: What the socket regulates with its own sensor: heating, cooling, humidifying, dehumidifying or CO₂ – then it switches at two points of the reading. With a timer it switches at set times of day, and Off keeps it off.

plugDayNight.title: Day and night
plugDayNight.text: The socket knows the day only as a time: it begins at “Day from” and ends at “Night from”, on your clock. With switch points of their own at night it regulates to other values at night; in CO₂ mode it does not dose at night at all.

switchPoints.title: Switch points
switchPoints.text: Two values rather than one target: at one the socket switches on, at the other off. The gap between them keeps it from switching back and forth with every reading – the wider it is, the less often it switches, and the further the reading swings.

timerWindows.title: Time windows
timerWindows.text: When the socket is on, the same every day: from a time of day for so many minutes. A window may run past midnight. The times are on your clock and move with daylight saving time.

fanMode.title: The fan runs
fanMode.text: Fixed: the AIR runs at one set speed by day and another at night. By temperature, humidity or both: it runs at its lowest speed while the reading stays under the target, and speeds up the further the reading rises above it – up to its highest speed. Day, for the AIR, is while its light sensor sees light.

fanSpeeds.title: Speed
fanSpeeds.text: As a share of full speed. In fixed mode one value holds by day and one at night. Regulated, the fan never runs slower than “At least” and never faster than “Most” – so the night stays quiet and the air still moves.

lightSchedule.title: Light
lightSchedule.text: When the lamp comes on and goes off, on your clock: the times move with daylight saving time. The brightness is the most it ramps up to. How long it fades in and out is under Advanced at the device.

modeNote.heater: For a heater: on once it is colder than the switch-on point, off above the switch-off point.

modeNote.temperature: Speeds up once it is warmer than 1 °C below the target temperature, and runs at its most 1 °C above it. The humidity below does not apply.
modeNote.humidity: Speeds up once the air is more humid than 5 % below the target humidity, and runs at its most 5 % above it. The temperature below does not apply.
